name: Nested Learning / Hope (Behrouz, Razaviyayn, Zhong, Mirrokni)
ontology_notes: Learning paradigm, not a companion store. Nested Learning treats a model as nested optimization problems, each with its own context flow. Continuum Memory System (CMS) is a chain of MLP blocks with different update frequencies. High-frequency blocks adapt fast and hold knowledge briefly. Low-frequency blocks hold more persistent knowledge. Hope is self-modifying Titans plus CMS. Hope-Attention replaces the Titans block with softmax attention. No user, character, relationship, lore, or OOC types.

ontology.evidence: Paper §7.1 formalizes CMS as MLP^(f_1)..MLP^(f_k) with chunk sizes from update frequency. Hope (§8) is self-modifying Titans followed by CMS. Kinds are frequency levels, not companion memory kinds.
ontology.label: measured

write_policy.evidence: Each level runs its own optimizer on its context flow. CMS updates only blocks whose scheduled frequency fires (paper §7.1). Hope learns its own update algorithm (self-referential Titans). No user pin. No joke refusal.
write_policy.label: measured

read_policy.evidence: Read is the sequence-model forward pass through Hope or Hope-Attention (Figure 5, §8.3). No retrieve-nothing gate for social silence. Memory is weights, not a queryable companion log.
read_policy.label: measured

supersession.evidence: Paper §7.1. When a higher-frequency MLP is overwritten, lower-frequency blocks can still hold the old knowledge, so forgotten content can be partly recovered. That is frequency-based retention, not typed fact supersession.
supersession.label: measured

temporal.evidence: Time is update frequency and chunk size C^(ℓ). Continual-translation and class-incremental setups use sequential tasks (Figure 6, Figure 8). No calendar last-Tuesday query.
temporal.label: measured

identity_split.evidence: One Hope backbone. No user vs character vs relationship objects.
identity_split.label: measured

silence.evidence: Eval retrieve is NIAH, LongHealth, QASPER, BABILong. No skip-a-relevant-memory control.
silence.label: measured

poisoning.evidence: Surprising or high-frequency context writes into CMS or Titans weights. No trust tags.
poisoning.label: inferred

forgetting.evidence: CMS is built so knowledge forgotten from MLP^(f_s) can remain in MLP^(f_s') with s'<s (paper §7.1). Optimizers also carry forget gates on momentum (paper §4). Not a user forget-that.
forgetting.label: measured

cost_shape.evidence: Paper §7.1. Average CMS update cost is O(1/f̂ × L_layer/5 × d_in^2) parameters per step because only due blocks update. Hope still trains from scratch on ~50B tokens for RULER/BABILong (§9.2). Steal the scheduled-update cost, not a companion API.
cost_shape.label: measured

local.evidence: NeurIPS 2025 paper HTML has no official GitHub. CC BY 4.0 on the PDF. Unofficial Hope reimplementations are not author code.
local.label: measured

mcp.evidence: Architecture paper. No MCP in https://arxiv.org/html/2512.24695.
mcp.label: measured

companion_fit_reason: Hope is a sequence architecture with continuum memory timescales. It is not a companion log or product memory API. Steal multi-timescale retention. Evals are continual classification, NIAH, BABILong, Wiki/commonsense, MAD. Those are not companion holes.

published_eval.name: Class-incremental CLINC/Banking/DBpedia, RULER MK-NIAH, LongHealth, QASPER, BABILong, WikiText plus commonsense (PIQA, HellaSwag, ARC, BoolQ), MAD, formal language recognition
published_eval.claimed_score: Hope  Wiki PPL 18.68, avg commonsense 52.28 (Table 2). Hope-3 recovers ICL on continual novel-language translation where ICL forgets (Figure 8). Hope holds BABILong further than Titans/ARMT past 1M, reported to 10M after fine-tune (§9.2).
published_eval.what_it_actually_scores: Continual classification, long-context retrieval/QA, next-token LM, and synthetic memorization. Not character drift, social silence, poisoning, or forget-that in a 1:1 companion.

open_unknowns: Whether official Hope training code will be released.
